original_concern.concern: The Definition says that holonomy around either meridian is conjugate to diag(i,−i), immediately after permitting a smooth O(2)-reduced A0 in A0+(1/4)diag(i,−i)dθ. Exact finite-loop holonomy does not follow from that hypothesis. Locally, A0=c diag(i,−i)(x dy−y dx) is smooth and preserves the reduction, but changes radius-r meridional holonomy to exp(±2πi(1/4+cr²)), generally not traceless. Specify limiting meridional holonomy, or impose an appropriate exact model near the link. The primary source explicitly discusses asymptotic holonomy in Proposition 3.2's proof: https://people.math.harvard.edu/~kronheim/khovanov-unknot.pdf, printed p.29.

cases.concrete_reason: The written smooth O(2)-reduced background need not be flat on a finite meridian. In the displayed abelian local test, xdy−ydx restricts to r²dtheta, so finite-radius holonomy is exp(±2pi i(1/4+cr²)); its conjugacy class need not be traceless. Smoothness instead makes the background contribution tend to zero as r tends to zero, so the limiting conjugacy class is correct. The proposed correction preserves the actual singular-residue/orbifold data. For flat connections homotopy invariance makes finite meridians conjugate to that limiting class, preserving the flat representation calculations.

replacements.source_excerpt: Parallel transport (holonomy) around either meridian is conjugate in $SU(2)$ to $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$; its image has order two in $PU(2)$.
replacements.proposed_replacement: As the radius of a meridional circle tends to zero, its holonomy conjugacy class tends to that of $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$ in $SU(2)$; the limiting image has order two in $PU(2)$. This is the prescribed asymptotic meridional holonomy, not an assertion of exact holonomy on every finite-radius circle for an arbitrary smooth $A_0$. For a flat connection the holonomies of homotopic meridional circles are conjugate, so their conjugacy class is exactly this limiting class.

original_concern.concern: The title and final Counterexample prose claim nonexistence of a locally finite translation-invariant reference, whereas steps 1.2–2.1 explicitly assume finiteness on every bounded Borel set. The stronger conclusion is true, but the reduction is omitted: local finiteness at 0 supplies a finite-mass ball B(0,R); place disjoint balls B((R/2)e_j,R/8) inside it, force their common mass to zero, and use a countable cover by balls of radius R/8. Include that reduction or otherwise justify the locally finite wording.

cases.concrete_reason: Finiteness on every bounded Borel set is stronger than local finiteness on a non-locally-compact Hilbert space. Existing proof only establishes the stronger-premise case, whereas the title/final assertion excludes every locally finite reference. The proposed proof chooses a finite-mass ball B(0,R), packs disjoint r=R/8 balls centered at(R/2)e_j in it, obtains their common mass zero, and covers ell² by countably many radius-r balls using the existing explicit dense set. It proves the full claimed locally-finite conclusion with the same Gaussian witness and no new supplier.

replacements.source_excerpt: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a translation-invariant Borel measure finite on every bounded Borel set. Put $U_j=\{x:\|x-e_j\|_2<1/3\}$. For $j\ne k$, $\|e_j-e_k\|_2=\sqrt2>2/3$, so the $U_j$ are pairwise disjoint. Each lies in the bounded ball $\{x:\|x\|_2<2\}$ by the triangle inequality. Translation invariance gives $\lambda(U_j)=m$ independent of $j$. If $m>0$, the first $N$ disjoint balls have total measure $Nm$ for every $N$, contradicting finiteness of the radius-two ball. Hence $m=0$. [F2, given, algebra]
replacements.proposed_replacement: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a nonzero locally finite translation-invariant Borel measure, where locally finite means that every point has a neighborhood of finite measure. At zero choose $R>0$ with $\lambda(B(0,R))<\infty$. Put $r=R/8$ and $U_j=B((R/2)e_j,r)$. For $j\ne k$ the distance between the centers is $R/\sqrt2>2r$, so these balls are pairwise disjoint, and every $U_j$ lies in $B(0,R)$ because $R/2+r<R$. Translation invariance gives a common finite mass $m=\lambda(U_j)$. If $m>0$, finite additivity and monotonicity give $Nm\le\lambda(B(0,R))$ for every $N$, a contradiction. Hence $m=0$. This covers in particular every measure finite on all bounded Borel sets, since that condition implies local finiteness. [F2, F4, given, algebra]

replacements.source_excerpt: 2.1 Translation invariance and step 1.2 make every radius-$1/3$ ball have measure zero. Let $D$ be the set of finitely supported rational sequences. [F3] makes $D$ countable: it is the countable union, over support lengths $N$, of the countable set $\mathbb Q^N$ padded with zeros. It is dense in $\ell^2$: for any $x\in\ell^2$ and $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ so that the squared tail sum is less than $\epsilon^2/4$, then approximate the first $N$ coordinates by rationals with squared total error less than $\epsilon^2/4$; the resulting padded vector is within $\epsilon$ of $x$. The radius-$1/3$ balls centered at $D$ therefore form a countable cover of $\ell^2$. By [F2], $\lambda(\ell^2)=0$, and [F4] makes every Borel subset null. This contradicts that $\lambda$ is nonzero. Hence no such reference measure exists, refuting the statement; in particular, the displayed Gaussian has no density relative to one. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, given, algebra, choose] ∎

The radius-$r$ balls centered at $D$ therefore form a countable cover of $\ell^2$. By [F2], $\lambda(\ell^2)=0$, and [F4] makes every Borel subset null. This contradicts that $\lambda$ is nonzero.
